transcript.text: Bosch induction hob PUE611BB1E making a loud buzzing/humming noise when I put my big stockpot on high. Is it about to break?

No, it is not about to break. What you are hearing is a very common and normal characteristic of induction hobs called magnetostriction. The coil inside the hob vibrates at high frequency when delivering maximum power, which creates a humming or buzzing sound that travels through your cookware. This effect is significantly louder with 'big stockpots' because they often have large flat bases that act like loudspeakers to amplify the vibration. It is also more noticeable if the pot has a thin base or if it is not perfectly level on the glass. As long as you do not hear any cracking, see sparks, smell burning plastic, or get an error code, your hob is functioning correctly and does not need repair.
[Safety panel] An appliance that keeps tripping your electrics — or that smells of burning or has scorch marks — may have an electrical fault. Stop using it, switch it off and unplug it, don't keep resetting it, and have it checked by a qualified electrician or appliance engineer.

reading.symptom: loud buzzing/humming noise when putting a big stockpot on high heat

plan: They asked: "Is it about to break?" - answer that first.
Already given by the customer, never ask for it again: make Bosch; model PUE611BB1E.
The fault they reported is: "loud buzzing/humming noise when putting a big stockpot on high heat". Keep to it: never describe a symptom, result or state they have not told you.

Stage 1 (broad help): say what could cause this, most likely first, as possibilities rather than certainties, including simple causes (settings, loading, detergent, installation, or normal behaviour) where they fit. Then give the one or two safe checks, or the one question, that would best tell those causes apart. Do not ask for the model number in this reply. Do not tell them to buy, order or replace a part yet.
